title.narrative: Activity under preparation Team Europe Skills Initiative: strengthening TVET for youth employment and Global Gateway Investments

description.narrative: Skills development is crucial to develop local economies and associated value chains. This is particularly important given that youth comprise more than 60% of Pakistan¿s population (64% under 30 years and 29% between 15 and 29) that could either turn into an asset or an emerging concern . With almost three million youth entering the labour market every year, millions of Pakistani youth face limited employment prospects. The action will support GG in Pakistan in two ways. Firstly, it will expand and consolidate the GG Flagship on TVET Centers of Excellence by strengthening the quality of education/skill training through investing in infrastructure, labour market analysis, teachers training and adequate teaching materials in the most fragile parts of the country (i.e., the provinces bordering Afghanistan: Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkwa and Gilgit Baltistan).. By doing so, it will provide better opportunities for decent employment for the youth in these regions. By investing in youth employability in these provinces, the action will also address migration by supporting skills training for returnees and refugees.The action consolidates and builds on the good work of previous EU support to TVET sector (development of National TVET policy, strategies and systems such as the National Vocational Qualifications Framework, Competency-Based Training and Recognition of Prior Learning). Building on these achievements for which the EU is recognised to have supported the transformation of the TVET sector in Pakistan, it will strengthen quality of TVET trainings, reinforce private sector engagement and make TVET even more market driven. Secondly, the action will support Pakistan to increase investments and their impact under the EU¿s GG strategy. The government has shown a strong interest to engage with EIB and other European international financial institutions (IFIs). Major investments are already planned in the energy and water sectors ¿ two sectors at the frontline of the green transition. However, the success and sustainability of these investments cannot be achieved without a skilled workforce. This action will use an ¿opportunity-driven approach¿ by flexibly following and supporting GG investments wherever they arise through accompanying skills development measures. More concretely, possible/relevant investment in skills and related value chain developments will be made to accompany and maximise impact of GG investments wherever in Pakistan they take place (this part of the action is thus not limited to the three regions covered by the above mentioned component). Skills-related investment barriers will be identified and addressed in partnership with business and investor networks, including the recently created ¿EU-Pakistan Business Network¿ that regroups the 300+ EU companies active in Pakistan. This cooperation will help align training with upcoming bankable green projects and access-to-finance instruments developed under the EFSD+ and SME greening programmes.In the context of Pakistan, the action will not only consolidate and expand the GG Flagship on ¿Climate-Resilient Infrastructure and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Centres in Pakistan¿ but also support the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) ¿Building Back Better through Green Jobs Creation'¿ through its strong partnership with Germany. The EU is considered as the largest donor in TVET in Pakistan.
